findings.title: A category added before first run stops the starting list for good: no Cash, Unaccounted or Salary, ever
findings.detail: `seed_categories()` seeds only when the person has **no** categories at all (D146 (3)). Someone with Capture who signs in from a plain browser is, by D146 (2), not sent to first run, and Settings → *Categories and rules* is open to them: it says *No categories yet · Categories show here once your first payment is in* and offers *Add a category*. Adding one (say *Pets*) means first run's `setup.start` later seeds nothing, so the person ends with one category: none of D33's list and none of the three Sen relies on (`system_key` salary, cash, unaccounted). B13's balance-check adjustments need Unaccounted and B10's salary cycles need Salary; nothing in the app can create them again. The empty state's words are also wrong for this person: categories come from first run, not from a first payment.
findings.repro: API: `category.add` (Pets) then `setup.start` as the same person (qa/B08/api-probes-r2.probe.ts › run 2: the seed). UI: FLOW-R2-12 — capture person in a browser, Settings → Categories → Add a category *Pets*, then open /s/first-run and continue.

findings.title: After first run is finished, /s/first-run still opens at *Step 2 of 7*
findings.detail: The router sends a person *to* first run until it's done, but nothing sends them *away* once it is: `FirstRun` renders the steps whatever `setupDone` says. findings.title: `GET /api/me` now costs four more database round trips: `setupDone` is read in a second transaction
findings.detail: Metrics flag `api:GET /api/me 200` api.queries 10 against main's 6. Cause, measured: the four extra statements are one more `asPerson` transaction (begin, `set_config('app.user_id', …)`, the `user_settings` select, commit) that `/me` opens after the access lookup's own, only to read `setup_done_at`. `/me` is read at every app start and by the router's first-run rule, and on Neon each round trip is a network hop. Folding the read into the transaction the request already has (or reading it with the access row) removes them.

findings.title: In a plain browser, a name typed offline at step 6 is lost, though the step says Next saves it
findings.detail: Offline, *Next* on *Your name* fires `setting.set`, which in a browser fails at once (toast *Couldn't save. Check your connection · Retry*) while first run moves on to step 7; after reconnecting and *Finish*, `own_names` is `{}` and only the payday was saved. A capture person isn't routed to first run in a browser (D146 (2)), and in the shell the write goes to the native outbox, which this cloud session can't run. So the routed path is untested: queued as phone step 8 in docs/local.md.
